topic: Function Pointer Arrays for Callback Dispatch
explanation: In advanced C programming, arrays of function pointers are used to implement flexible callback mechanisms, dispatch tables, or plugin architectures. This technique allows dynamic selection and invocation of functions at runtime, enabling highly modular and extensible code. It is particularly useful in scenarios requiring efficient event handling, command dispatching, or implementing state machines without resorting to complex switch-case statements.
code_example: void callbackA(int x) { printf("Callback A: %d\n", x); }
void callbackB(int x) { printf("Callback B: %d\n", x); }
int index = 1; // dynamically determined at runtime
example_explanation: This example defines an array of function pointers 'callbacks' pointing to two functions 'callbackA' and 'callbackB'. By selecting an index at runtime, the program dynamically dispatches the appropriate callback function, demonstrating how arrays of function pointers enable flexible, efficient callback mechanisms in advanced C programming.
